Petitioners-accused Nos.2 to 4 along with accused No.1 have been charge sheeted for the offences under Sections 498A, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961,
alleging that, the defacto-complainant is the legal wedded wife of accused No.1, and accused Nos.2 &
3 are parents-in-law, and accused No.4 is the relative of the accused No.1-husband, and they subjected her to cruelty, both mentally & physically and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home failing which, accused No.1 would divorce her and contract another marriage.
2.

The cognizance of the aforesaid offences taken by learned Magistrate is impugned in this petition by accused Nos.2 to 4.
3.

sentences.text: He further submits that the FIR clearly discloses that the petitioners were staying separately, and not in the matrimonial home of the defacto-complainant.
He submits that the cognizance taken was only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations.
In the absence of any corroborative material, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.
4. Respondent No.2-defacto-complainant though served with notice has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.

5. Learned HCGP appearing for the respondent- State submits that, the charge sheet material discloses the offences alleged against the petitioners-accused, and the veracity of the allegations can be gone into only after full fledge trial, and at this stage, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate does not warrant interference.
6. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties.

7. In the FIR, respondent No.2 has alleged that two years back accused No.1 went to his native place stating that, he would get money from his mother Padmavathi i.e., accused No.2 and clear all the debts.

Unfortunately, he did not turn back to Bangalore, and she had to face hardship and with the help of her parents & god's grace she started working and taking care of her child and she is staying with the parents.
8. It was further alleged that accused No.1 has contracted second marriage at the instance of his parents i.e., accused Nos.2 & 3.

This clearly establishes that the accused herein were not staying at the matrimonial home of accused No.1 and the defacto-complainant and they were staying separately, and expect omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation, as against the petitioners-accused herein.

FIR was lodged after two years from the date of the last incident,
without offering any plausible explanation which clearly implies that the FIR was lodged with malne and without probable cause.

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar at para No.18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in- laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

The charge sheet material does not disclose the prima facie case against the petitioners-accused herein, and the continuation of the criminal proceedings would be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER a) Criminal petition is allowed.
b) The impugned proceedings in CC No.26805/2016 on the file of XXXI Additional Chief Magistrate, Bangalore in so far as it relates to accused Nos.2 to 4 is hereby quashed.
